exposure: Mode of delivery (vaginal vs. cesarean section)
cohort: 106 term newborns - 40 born vaginally, 51 born via cesarean section with spinal anesthesia, and 15 born via cesarean section with general anesthesia
finding: Newborns born vaginally had significantly higher rectal temperatures compared to those born via cesarean section, with the lowest temperatures observed in the general anesthesia group.
mod_finding: Newborns delivered via cesarean section had lower rectal temperatures compared to those delivered vaginally.
